newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil slips as market braces for Iraqi exports.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil slips as market braces for Iraqi exports.

text.p: Oil traders on Wednesday were bracing for a renewed wave of Iraqi oil exports which analysts said would spell the end of a rally on world crude markets.
Prices would probably prove resilient in the short term but they warned of a looming imbalance on oil markets in the months ahead.
"Once the August demand peak passes, rising supply will be the dominant force affecting price dynamics," said consultants Petroleum Finance Corp.

Iraqi Oil Minister Mohammed Rasheed told reporters in Baghdad he expected exports to resume by mid-August after the final piece of the jigsaw for sales to restart fell into place at the United Nations on Tuesday.
Oil traders anticipated the first Iraqi cargoes arriving earlier, and were expecting liftings from the Turkish pipeline outlet of Ceyhan or Iraq's Gulf port Mina al-Bakr within a few days.
London September North Sea Brent blend futures closed 34 cents lower at $19.18 a barrel. Brent has recovered from its low for the year at $17.30 in early June.
Dealers said strong U.S. demand and a recent series of oilfield and refinery supply disruptions which have capped summer stockbuilds would keep a floor under oil prices for the time being.
"Iraq will definitely dampen the market down but prices are unlikely to fall much immediately," said a London-based oil analyst.
"I think traders will want to see physical evidence of Iraqi crude actually in the market."
"The market will be able to take it without really struggling," said Nigel Saperia at Bankers Trust. "Once people start hedging the Iraqi oil it will weaken. But I don't think it will set new lows."
Sales under the second phase of Iraq's oil-for-food exchange with the U.N. were delayed since early June by negotiations over an aid distribution plan.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) agreed on Tuesday with U.N. oil sale overseers new crude price formulas which should be rubber-stamped by U.N. authorities in two days.
Iraq is now expected to move full steam ahead in an effort to meet its permitted $2.14 billion worth of sales, including $140 million for Turkish pipeline fees, in two equal 90-day instalments.
It will have only a month to reach an initial billion dollar target by September 5 which analysts say will prove beyond its export capacity.
Key to the oil markets in the short term will be Iraqi export capacity. Analysts estimate Iraq is capable of moving some 1.3-1.4 million bpd. Baghdad says capacity stands at 1.8 million bpd.
